page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz. It provisions 2 physical cores, translating to 4 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields a standardized ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, targeting balanced multi-tasking and baseline compute requirements.

Hardware capabilities omit local disk storage, indicating that the VM requires remote block volumes or network-attached storage for operating system images and persistent data. The instance also features zero hardware accelerators, with a GPU count of 0.0, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for direct network ingress and egress. Because hardware threads are dedicated rather than shared, performance remains steady across persistent workloads.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of AMD EPYC processing cores and standard memory allocation delivers a cost-efficient resource footprint for mainstream tasks without incurring expenses associated with unused local NVMe drives or specialized GPU silicon. Workload profiles well-aligned with this instance include intermediate web servers, backend application microservices, development and testing environments, continuous integration agents, and small-scale relational or in-memory databases.
